overview: Trengwainton is a National Trust garden in Madron, just outside Penzance, with views out over Mount’s Bay to the Lizard. It’s famous for its rare and exotic trees and shrubs, which thrive in the mild far-west climate. (The house itself is private.)
Its old walled gardens are a quirk of history: built in Elizabethan times, probably to protect fruit trees during a long spell of colder weather, their walls held in the warmth on chilly nights.

expect.title: Exotic planting
expect.text: Rare trees and shrubs from around the world fill the garden.

expect.title: The walled gardens
expect.text: Historic walled gardens built to shelter frost-tender plants.

expect.title: The view
expect.text: Look out across Mount’s Bay towards the Lizard.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry for non-members; National Trust members get in free.

goodToKnow.label: Before you go
goodToKnow.text: Check the National Trust website for opening times.

week.text: A lovely gentle visit near Penzance, at its most colourful in spring. Pair it with Trewidden, another garden nearby, or Penlee House gallery in town.

pairWith.why: another garden a couple of kilometres away
the main town for food and shops

tips: Visit in spring for the flowering shrubs at their most colourful.
